title: Milei Approval Rating Rebounds From Lowest Point as Inflation Concerns Ease
detail: Bloomberg reported a recovery in President Milei's approval rating from its lowest point, tied to slowly easing inflation concerns ahead of the October 26, 2026 midterm elections. Annual inflation stands near 32.4% as of April 2026, down sharply from the 211.4% peak in December 2023. The approval recovery strengthens Milei's La Libertad Avanza (LLA) position for midterms, in which the party seeks congressional gains to advance structural reforms — including a Super RIGI investment bill and a lobbying-transparency law — without dependence on fragile coalition partners.

media.caption: Milei's approval rating rebounds ahead of October 2026 midterm elections

title: Milei Austerity Strips Therapy and Support Funding from 5 Million Argentines with Disabilities
detail: The Washington Post reported that the Milei government cut therapy and support funding for an estimated 5 million Argentines with disabilities as part of broader fiscal austerity measures. The cuts drew international attention to the social cost of Milei's budget consolidation program, which achieved a primary fiscal surplus of 1.9% of GDP in 2024 but through deep cuts to health, education, and disability services. Critics warned the measures would strip essential services from Argentina's most vulnerable populations.

media.caption: Disabled Argentines face loss of essential services under Milei austerity program

title: Photographer Injured by Tear Gas at Weekly Retirees' Protest Outside Congress
detail: Photographer Antonio Becerra from Tiempo Argentino was injured by tear gas fired by federal security forces during the weekly retirees' protest in front of the National Congress in Buenos Aires. RSF (Reporters Without Borders) documented the incident, noting that retirees have held weekly protests at Congress since February 19, 2026, opposing pension cuts under the Milei government's fiscal adjustment program. This incident, combined with the May 21 arrest of photographer Tomás Cuesta, prompted RSF to issue a formal warning about Argentina's deteriorating press freedom trajectory.

media.caption: RSF warns of escalating media repression at Buenos Aires retirees' protests
